messages:
Janet (OrbitPay): Hey team — starting ~09:03 UTC we saw a spike of failed payments and weird NLP output. Our app calls redwood-2b for invoice summarization but some requests returned much shorter, garbled text and different token counts. Also saw 403s intermittently. Can we investigate?

Rebecca - Support: Sorry about that, Janet. Can you paste one example request_id and the raw request (headers + body) if possible? Any repro steps?

Janet (OrbitPay): request_id: req_2026-03-17_09:03:47_a1f2
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-orbitpay' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: req_2026-03-17_09:03:47_a1f2' \
  -H 'X-Region-Preference: us-west' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","input":"Summarize invoice 0x12..."}'

Janet (OrbitPay): Note: in logs we saw a 403 then a 200 but body looked like a much smaller model (short replies, emojis removed). Billing shows duplicate token charge for the same request_id.

region-router-bot: Automatic route decision: client=sk-orbitpay ip=3.120.45.6 reason=auth-probe fallback_region=eu-west-standby routed_variant=redwood-lite-v0.9

Tom - Eng Oncall: @Rebecca @Anna thanks — initial guess: auth probe triggered fallback to standby region which is running a lighter variant (redwood-lite-v0.9) without the same tokenizer/vocab. That would explain shorter outputs and token count diffs. 403s could be from token validation hitting a regional auth proxy.

Rebecca - Support: Ok. Janet, can you confirm the Authorization header TTL or whether you rotated keys around that time? Also did you see long tail latency before the 403s?

Janet (OrbitPay): No key rotate. Latency spiked ~350ms to 1.2s before error. We did not set X-Region-Preference previously but added it today for testing.

Anna - Infra SRE: I'm pulling router logs now. Command: 
```
kubectl logs -l app=region-router -n prod --since=15m | grep req_2026-03-17_09:03:47_a1f2 -n
```
Found sequence: auth-probe -> route-eval -> capacity-fallback -> route: eu-west-standby -> served by host eu-west-02 -> variant redwood-lite-v0.9

Tom - Eng Oncall: Can we prod the variant mapping? I want to see what model families are allowed as fallbacks for redwood-2b. If the mapping mistakenly includes lite variants, that's the bug.

Anna - Infra SRE: Mapping dump (sanitized):
```
{ "primary": "redwood-2b", "fallbacks": ["redwood-2b-quant", "redwood-lite-v0.9", "redwood-2b-compat"] }
```
That explains it — fallback list contains the lite variant. This is an ops config regression from the last deploy.

Rebecca - Support: We'll escalate to Config and Routing. Janet — for now you can pin requests to region us-west and strict variant using header X-Force-Variant: redwood-2b to avoid fallback. Example: 
```
-H 'X-Force-Variant: redwood-2b'
```
But we should fix the fallback config so routes never map redwood-2b -> redwood-lite-v0.9.

Lex - Billing: Janet, about the duplicate token charge — we saw a retry path when the auth-probe caused a 403, the client retried and the standby returned a shorter but billable response. We have two billable events linked to the same X-Request-ID across regions. We'll refund the extra charge pending root cause. Please share invoice id if you want immediate credit.

Janet (OrbitPay): Thanks Lex. Please refund invoice INV-2026-0317-999 and escalate the quality/regression — customers noticed missing important invoice lines.

Tom - Eng Oncall: Root cause summary so far: (1) auth-probe to regional standby erroneously allowed routing to a lite variant; (2) lite variant uses different tokenizer -> tokenization drift and truncation; (3) client retried after 403 -> duplicate billing. Action items: roll back recent routing/config change, add unit test to prevent lite variants in fallback lists for mainline models, add guard that rejects variant mismatch (model_family != requested_family) on standby routes, and add billing dedupe on X-Request-ID across regions.

Anna - Infra SRE: Rolling rollback now (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-17-09-15). Will post status.

region-router-bot: Rollback started: deploy-2026-03-17-09-15 -> target=region-router config v42 -> status=initiated

Rebecca - Support: Janet, once rollback completes I'll monitor and re-run your sample request with a support token to confirm behavior. Also we'll coordinate refund. Sorry for the disruption. :pray:

Janet (OrbitPay): Appreciate the quick turn. One ask: could we get a postmortem or short blameless summary once fixed? This caused visible customer impact.

Tom - Eng Oncall: Absolutely. We'll schedule a short blameless postmortem and add replay cases to our e2e to catch tokenizer drift on fallback.

Anna - Infra SRE: Rollback complete -> status=success. Router mapping no longer lists redwood-lite-v0.9 for redwood-2b.

region-router-bot: Route config applied: v41 restored. All traffic from orbitpay tokens should resume normal routing.

Rebecca - Support: Janet — can you re-run the original curl and paste the response? If all good we'll close.

Janet (OrbitPay): Re-ran at 09:21 UTC, got 200 with expected long summary. No duplicate billing now visible. Thanks everyone, please keep me posted about the postmortem.

Lex - Billing: Refund processed for INV-2026-0317-999 (credit id: cred_2026-03-17_01).

Tom - Eng Oncall: Follow-ups created: ROUTE-457 (remove lite variants from critical fallback sets), BILL-312 (dedupe X-Request-ID cross-region), QA-88 (e2e fallback tokenizer check). Closing thread after PM posts postmortem.

Rebecca - Support: Closing now but leaving PM for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
